records.title: About
records.summary: What Our West Valley AZ is and how it works.
records.text: About What Our West Valley AZ is and how it works. Our West Valley AZ is an independent, noncommercial civic information project for Arizona's West Valley. It is not affiliated with the City of Avondale or any other government agency. Why OWVAZ exists Useful local government information is often spread across city websites, budgets, meeting portals, agendas, reports, and other public records. OWVAZ organizes that information around what residents are trying to find and explains it in plain language. Find it. Understand it. Go to the source if you want more. How information is researched OWVAZ takes accuracy seriously and prefers authoritative primary sources such as official government websites, adopted budgets, agendas, minutes, resolutions, contracts, and public records. Important factual claims should be traceable to identifiable evidence. Summaries and explanations are intended to make source material easier to understand, not to replace the underlying records. When an official source or service is available, OWVAZ links residents directly to it. When available evidence does not establish something, OWVAZ aims to identify that limitation rather than fill the gap with an assumption. Editorial independence OWVAZ is independently operated. It is not operated by or on behalf of a city, government agency, political candidate, campaign, political party, or government contractor. The project is noncommercial and is intended to help residents find, understand, and verify information about their communities. Use of artificial intelligence OWVAZ may use artificial intelligence tools to assist with organizing, comparing, summarizing, researching, and presenting information. AI tools may also assist with technical work involved in developing and maintaining the website. AI output is not treated as an authoritative source. Factual claims published by OWVAZ are expected to be supported by underlying records or other identifiable sources, and important claims should be verified against those sources whenever practical. Corrections Accuracy is an ongoing responsibility. When reliable information shows that OWVAZ has published a factual error or that important context is missing, OWVAZ aims to correct or clarify the information. Residents are encouraged to provide corrections and supporting sources through the Contact page. Privacy OWVAZ is designed so residents can use the site without being tracked or profiled by OWVAZ. The current site does not require resident accounts and is designed without advertising, tracking pixels, behavioral analytics, browser or device fingerprinting, or third party social trackers. Site searches run in the resident's browser. Read the OWVAZ Privacy page for details about search, cookies, browser storage, external links, and the site's privacy by design approach.

records.title: Disclaimer
records.summary: Important information about using Our West Valley AZ.
records.text: Disclaimer Important information about using Our West Valley AZ. Our West Valley AZ is an independent, noncommercial civic information project. It is not a government agency, is not affiliated with the City of Avondale or any other government agency, and is not an official government record or service. Last updated: September 8, 2026. Accuracy, sources, interpretation, and verification OWVAZ takes accuracy seriously. Information is researched and organized using public records, official government sources, and other authoritative sources whenever practical. Important factual claims are expected to be supported by identifiable evidence. OWVAZ may summarize, organize, categorize, compare, or explain public records and other source material. Those explanations are not themselves official government records and should be read together with the identified sources when the distinction matters. Reasonable people can sometimes interpret the same record or collection of records differently. OWVAZ aims to distinguish documented facts from interpretation and to identify material uncertainty when the available evidence does not establish a conclusion. AI output is not treated as an authoritative source. Public information can also change after publication. When a current deadline, legal requirement, eligibility determination, or other time sensitive official information matters, residents should confirm the current information with the responsible agency or authoritative source. Proposals, budgets, and public records OWVAZ distinguishes between what public records document and what those records do not establish. A proposal, budget request, appropriation, planned purchase, or similar record does not by itself prove that a project, purchase, policy, system, or deployment was ultimately completed or put into use. When the available public record does not establish a fact, OWVAZ aims to say so rather than fill the gap with an assumption. Completeness OWVAZ works to identify and explain useful public information, but the site may not contain every relevant record, update, event, agency action, or development. The absence of information from OWVAZ should not by itself be treated as evidence that an event, action, record, purchase, decision, or other development did not occur. Inclusion does not imply wrongdoing or endorsement The inclusion or discussion of a person, public official, organization, business, expenditure, contract, technology, proposal, investigation, government action, or public record on OWVAZ does not by itself imply wrongdoing, misconduct, endorsement, criticism, affiliation, or any conclusion beyond what the cited information supports. Likewise, linking to, quoting, or identifying an external person, organization, agency, business, or source does not by itself mean that OWVAZ or its operator endorses or is affiliated with that person or entity. External sources and links OWVAZ links to government agencies, public documents, meeting systems, utilities, and other external sources so residents can review information at its source. OWVAZ does not operate or control those external resources. External websites and documents can change, move, become unavailable, or contain information that OWVAZ has not independently verified. Reliance, professional information, and emergencies OWVAZ provides civic information to help residents understand their communities and locate authoritative sources. Residents remain responsible for decisions they make based on information obtained from OWVAZ or from sources linked by OWVAZ. OWVAZ does not provide legal, financial, medical, or other professional advice. Information involving legal rights, deadlines, eligibility, emergency services, financial decisions, or other consequential matters should be confirmed with the responsible agency or a qualified professional when appropriate. OWVAZ is not an emergency service. For emergencies, use the appropriate official emergency service. No professional or official relationship Using OWVAZ does not create an attorney client, financial advisory, medical, fiduciary, governmental, or other professional relationship between a resident and OWVAZ or its operator. OWVAZ does not act on behalf of a government agency merely because it provides, summarizes, or links to government information. Corrections OWVAZ aims to correct factual errors when reliable information shows that a published statement is inaccurate or incomplete. Residents are encouraged to provide corrections and supporting sources through the Contact page. Responsibility for external changes and consequential reliance OWVAZ and its operator are not responsible for changes made by government agencies or other third parties after OWVAZ information was researched or published, or for an external website, document, service, or resource being changed, moved, or made unavailable. To the extent permitted by applicable law, OWVAZ and its operator are not responsible for losses resulting from a person's failure to verify time sensitive or consequential information with the responsible authoritative source when such verification is appropriate.

records.title: Privacy
records.summary: How Our West Valley AZ protects resident privacy.
records.text: Privacy How Our West Valley AZ protects resident privacy. Our West Valley AZ is designed around a simple privacy principle: residents should be able to access civic information without being tracked, profiled, or required to identify themselves to OWVAZ. Last updated: September 8, 2026. What OWVAZ does not use The OWVAZ website is designed without: resident accounts advertising networks behavioral analytics tracking pixels browser or device fingerprinting third party social trackers third party analytics scripts third party advertising scripts persistent browser storage for tracking or profiling OWVAZ does not sell resident information or use the website to build advertising, behavioral, or personal profiles of visitors. Cookies and browser storage The current OWVAZ site code does not set cookies and does not use localStorage, sessionStorage, or IndexedDB to identify, track, or profile residents. If a future feature requires cookies or persistent browser storage, its privacy impact must be evaluated before that feature is added and this page must be updated when appropriate. Search privacy OWVAZ search is designed to operate in the resident's browser. When a resident searches OWVAZ, the site loads static OWVAZ search index data from the same website and performs the search locally in the browser. The search form does not submit the resident's search terms to OWVAZ, a search engine, an analytics provider, or another third party search service. Loading a search index is a normal request for a static website file. The resident's typed search term is not included in that request. Forms and information residents submit The current public site does not provide a contact form or other form that submits personal information to OWVAZ. The forms currently present on the site are search interfaces and do not have a network submission endpoint. If OWVAZ later adds a way for residents to submit corrections, sources, questions, or other information, the privacy implications and handling of that information will be documented before or when that feature is made available. External links OWVAZ links to official government agencies, public meeting systems, utilities, public documents, and other external sources. Following one of those links takes the resident to a website that OWVAZ does not operate or control. That external site may have its own cookies, analytics, logging, privacy practices, or terms. OWVAZ does not treat a link to an external website as permission for that site to track residents through OWVAZ. External resources are linked rather than automatically embedded whenever practical so residents can choose whether to visit them. Website requests and infrastructure Like any website, OWVAZ must receive a network request in order to send a requested page or file to a visitor's browser. That request can inherently include technical information needed for normal Internet communication, such as an IP address and basic request information. OWVAZ does not intend to use website infrastructure to track or profile residents. The production hosting, web server, reverse proxy, CDN, and related infrastructure configuration will be evaluated separately for request logging and data retention behavior. OWVAZ will not claim that no infrastructure level logs exist unless that has been verified. Privacy by design Privacy is treated as a design constraint rather than an optional feature. New analytics, tracking, advertising, profiling, third party embeds, or similar technologies are not assumed to be acceptable merely because they are common on other websites. If OWVAZ considers adding a feature that changes how resident information is handled, its purpose and privacy impact should be evaluated first. Changes to this privacy information OWVAZ's privacy practices and this page should be reviewed when a material change affects how resident or visitor information is handled. If OWVAZ adds a feature, service, or production technology that materially changes the privacy practices described here, this page should be updated to reflect that change.

records.title: Police Surveillance Technology
records.summary: Documented Avondale Police Department license plate readers, drones, body-worn cameras, and regional data-sharing systems.
records.text: Police Surveillance Technology Documented Avondale Police Department license plate readers, drones, body-worn cameras, and regional data-sharing systems. Avondale Police Department records document several technologies used to collect, search, share, or review information for law enforcement purposes. These include license plate reader cameras, police drones, body worn cameras, and regional data sharing systems. This page separates what City records currently document from proposals or details that have not yet been verified . {{ }} License plate readers Current system documented by the City The FY2027 City Manager's Recommended Budget states that Avondale Police Department operates 15 license plate reader (LPR) cameras throughout the city . The document says officers and dispatchers use the cameras to identify and query vehicles associated with crimes and calls for service. It also states that the camera database allows personnel to search for vehicles through cameras shared by more than 140 law enforcement agencies nationwide . The City describes real time alerts associated with categories including missing persons, vehicles used in felonies, stolen vehicles, stolen license plates, and other law enforcement alerts. Proposed FY2027 expansion The FY2027 recommended budget requested 58 additional license plate reader cameras . The stated purpose was to increase the number of cameras to provide citywide coverage in areas where cameras were not already present . The request was: $239,000 ongoing $0 one time $239,000 total annual request The FY2027 tentative budget continued to list the same 58 camera request and amount. Earlier LPR history Avondale's documented use of license plate reader technology predates the current program. A historical City budget describes implementation and training for an LPR system around 2008. The document says external cameras could read and store license plates and reports that approximately 50,000 plates had been collected during an early deployment period. The FY2023 final budget later reported that the Police Department had launched a license plate reader program and used it to identify two stolen vehicles. Because older City records already document LPR use, OWVAZ does not interpret the FY2023 wording as evidence that FY2023 was Avondale's first ever use of license plate readers. The FY2025 final budget also describes testing cameras functioning as license plate readers at intersections. The City says these cameras capture an image of vehicles passing through an intersection and can notify police when a vehicle of interest passes a monitored location. Police drones Avondale had an established police drone program before the FY2027 budget cycle. The FY2022 final budget documents a new drone program and says seven staff members were trained as licensed drone pilots. The FY2023 final budget reports that two additional drones were added. By the FY2027 recommended budget, the Police Department described a program consisting of 16 drones assigned to officers who had completed FAA training and received drone pilot licenses. Drone as First Responder The FY2027 recommended budget describes a proposed Drone as First Responder (DFR) model. The City's description involves a drone stored in an enclosed rooftop docking station that could be deployed by trained personnel to calls for service. The document says the system could provide information to responding officers before or during their arrival. The FY2027 supplemental request summary lists a $120,000 one time Public Safety Drone Program request. Body worn cameras Avondale Police Department's command staff page explicitly refers to an Axon Body Worn Camera Program . This establishes Axon in connection with Avondale's body worn camera program. It does not establish that Axon supplies Avondale's license plate readers or drone systems. FY2027 budget materials also contain a separate $25,000 ongoing request for body worn camera redaction software . Regional and interagency data sharing The FY2026 final budget reports that Avondale assigned one full time dispatcher to the West Valley Real Time Crime Center . Separately, the FY2027 recommended budget describes a Police Data Sharing request of: $75,000 ongoing $28,000 one time $103,000 total The City describes the proposed system as a nationwide data integration platform intended to combine otherwise separate law enforcement records into a searchable system and support interagency information sharing. OWVAZ does not currently treat the Police Data Sharing system, the West Valley Real Time Crime Center, and the 140 plus agency LPR camera database as the same system. The public records establish these facts separately. {{ }} What the public record does not yet show The earlier 58 camera LPR request and the final budget's State RICO funding assignment are both documented at $239,000 . The matching amounts do not, by themselves, establish that the final State RICO funding paid for the earlier 58 camera request. Public records reviewed by OWVAZ do not yet establish the following details: the vendor operating or supplying Avondale's current LPR network, the contract or purchase order for the current LPR system, the procurement vehicle for the proposed 58 camera expansion, the precise retention period for LPR records, the City's detailed LPR access and audit policy, the formal data sharing agreement governing the LPR network, the vendor for the proposed DFR system, the final deployment status of the 58 camera expansion, the final deployment status of DFR, or the exact vendor or product behind the FY2027 Police Data Sharing request. These details will remain unidentified unless supported by additional public records.
